argument_macro_structure.dominant_argument_form: Transcendental argument combined with reductio ad absurdum
argument_macro_structure.premise_explicitness: Moderate - premises are stated but often embedded in rhetorical prose rather than formal notation

argumentative_quality.dialectical_reasonableness: High - engages with potential objections (heteronomy, secularity) and addresses them systematically
argumentative_quality.logical_relevance: High - all sections directly serve the central thesis about the necessity of the divine postulate
argumentative_quality.premise_acceptability: Moderate - relies on Kantian premises that are contested (e.g., the fact of reason, the nature of conscience as tribunal)

distinctions_drawn: Objective vs. subjective condition of morality
Legislative vs. adjudicative function of conscience
Ex ante vs. ex post facto judgment
Source of law vs. guarantor of justice
explicit_definitions_given: Categorical Imperative - the universal, rational law that defines duty
Conscience - the internal, felt application of the moral law to individual actions
Postulate - a necessary condition of practical possibility, not a theoretical assertion
Pointless contradiction - a judgment that claims objective validity but lacks any external referent

dialectical_engagement.objection_handling: Explicitly addresses the objection that the argument reduces Kant's secular ethics to covert theology; responds by distinguishing postulates from theoretical assertions and clarifying that God is guarantor, not source, of the moral law
objections_raised: The argument reduces Kant's rigorous secular ethics to covert theology
The argument undermines the autonomy of the will
A naturalistic account of conscience (evolutionary psychology, social conditioning) could explain guilt without divine reference

epistemic_stance_and_voice.certainty_language_frequency: Moderate - uses phrases like 'logically necessitates,' 'must believe,' 'cannot stand alone' but also acknowledges interpretive claims

appeals_to_authority: Kant - Critique of Practical Reason (doctrine of postulates, Highest Good)
Kant - Religion within the Bounds of Bare Reason (conscience as representative of God)
method_and_evidence.evidence_type: Textual interpretation combined with a constructed thought experiment (Willie case) used as a test case for the theory
named_thought_experiments: The Willie case - a soldier forced to choose between obedience to lawful authority and preserving an innocent life

philosophical_orientation.grounding: Kantian - explicitly builds on Kant's moral philosophy, the Categorical Imperative, and the doctrine of postulates
philosophical_orientation.sentiment: Analytic and constructive - aims to identify a structural flaw in Kant's system and resolve it through a sympathetic extension of Kantian resources
philosophical_orientation.thematic_focus: Metaethics, moral psychology, philosophy of religion, normative ethics (moral dilemmas)

structural_organization.structure_type: Six-part progressive argument: (I) Objective foundation, (II) Subjective condition, (III) Test case, (IV) Identification of contradiction, (V) Resolution via postulate, (VI) Defense and evaluation, followed by a conclusion synthesizing the argument

summary_of_core_decisions: The text argues that Kant's dual structure of morality—objective CI and subjective conscience—contains a fatal flaw when confronted with tragic moral dilemmas. The Willie case shows that conscience condemns regardless of choice, creating a 'pointless contradiction': a verdict that claims objective validity but lacks any external referent. The resolution is the postulate of God as the ultimate judge, which transforms conscience from a self-referential psychological mechanism into a meaningful representation of divine judgment. This is not heteronomy because God is the guarantor of justice, not the source of the law. The argument concludes that the subjective condition of morality (conscience) logically requires the objective, transcendent anchor of the divine postulate to prevent moral accountability from dissolving into mere psychological description.

thesis_commitment.conclusion_type: Necessity claim - the divine postulate is logically required to resolve the internal contradiction of Kant's system
thesis_commitment.hedging_density_in_final_paragraph: Low - the conclusion is stated with confidence: 'logically culminates in the necessity of a divine tribunal'
